Languages
Compiled solvers, interpreted glue, and hardware that keeps changing
Compiled, interpreted, in between
Compiled
Source → compiler → machine code, then run
Good at: tight loops over millions of cells
Examples: Fortran, C, C++ · mf6, WRF, SUMMA
Just-in-time
Compiled the first time a function runs
Good at: speed without leaving an interactive session
Examples: Julia, JAX, Numba, Javascript
Interpreted
Read and run line by line, at a prompt
Good at: exploring, plotting, gluing tools together
Examples: Base Python, R, MATLAB
The two-language problem: researchers end up “coding algorithms in one programming language, only to have to rewrite them in a faster one.”
Perkel (2019), Nature 572:141–142, doi:10.1038/d41586-019-02310-3

GPUs reopen the question
E3SM EAMxx
Route: rewrite Fortran in C++ with Kokkos
Result: 8–30× faster; over 1 simulated year per day at 3.25 km on Frontier
E3SM project (2022, 2023)
Oceananigans.jl
Route: new model in Julia, GPU-first
Result: about 10 simulated years per day at 1/12° on 64 A100 GPUs
Silvestri et al. (2025), JAMES
NeuralGCM
Route: differentiable dynamical core in JAX, plus learned physics
Result: 70,000 simulated days in 24 hours on one TPU
Kochkov et al. (2024), Nature 632
Hardware changes within years; model codes live for decades. Separate the science from the hardware tuning.
Lawrence et al. (2018), Geosci. Model Dev. 11:1799–1821

Six lines of xarray - more on that next semester
import xarray as xr
ds = xr.open_dataset("forcing.nc", chunks={}) # lazy: dask arrays
pr = ds["pr"] # daily precipitation, mm
monthly = pr.resample(time="MS").sum() # monthly totals
box = monthly.sel(lat=slice(31.5, 33.0), lon=slice(-111.5, -110.0))
box.mean(["lat", "lon"]).plot() # area mean, drawn by matplotlib
Named dimensions
Select by lat and time, not by column 120
Lazy by default
Reads metadata now, data only when needed
NetCDF and Zarr
Follows the CF data model our forcing already uses

Scaling out: dask and Pangeo
Files
NetCDF or Zarr, on disk or in the cloud
→
Chunks
Each array split into blocks that fit in memory
→
Task graph
Operations recorded, not yet run
→
Workers
Laptop cores, HPC nodes or cloud machines run it
Pangeo
A community, not a package: xarray, dask, Jupyter and Zarr for big geoscience data, with compute placed next to the data (Abernathey et al. 2021, CiSE)
Cloud-native formats
Zarr stores chunked arrays as cloud objects (OGC community standard, 2022); VirtualiZarr reads existing NetCDF chunks without copying them
NumPy: ~1.04 billion downloads in 30 days (pepy.tech, Oct 2026) · xarray: ~10.4 million a month (pypistats.org, Nov 2026)

Licenses and citation
MIT
Short and permissive; keep the copyright notice
BSD-3-Clause
Like MIT, and no endorsement in the authors’ names
Apache-2.0
Permissive, with an explicit patent grant
GPL-3.0
Copyleft: shared derivatives stay GPL, with source
No license means all rights reserved: nobody can legally reuse your code, however public the repo.
CITATION.cff
A file in the repo that adds “Cite this repository” to GitHub, with APA and BibTeX
Zenodo DOI
Archives each GitHub release with its own DOI, plus one that always points to the latest

21
Be FAIR and CARE
FAIR · about the data
F
Findable: persistent identifiers, rich indexed metadata
A
Accessible: retrievable by identifier over open protocols
I
Interoperable: shared vocabularies and formats, like NetCDF-CF
R
Reusable: clear license, provenance, community standards
Wilkinson et al. (2016), Scientific Data 3:160018
CARE · about people and purpose
C
Collective benefit: data systems that let Indigenous Peoples benefit
A
Authority to control: the right to govern their own data
R
Responsibility: show how the use supports Indigenous Peoples
E
Ethics: rights and wellbeing first, across the data lifecycle
Carroll et al. (2020), Data Science Journal 19:43
Local relevance: Arizona has 22 federally recognized tribes. CARE’s lead author, Stephanie Russo Carroll, is at UA’s Native Nations Institute.

Packages and environments
Getting the same versions of everything, on every machine, next year too
Why environments exist
One global Python
Thesis project pins numpy 1.26
This course needs numpy 2.x
Result: installing one silently breaks the other
→
One environment per project
thesis: numpy 1.26, frozen for the paper
hwrs564a: numpy 2.x, flopy, mf6
Result: each rebuilt from one file
A computational environment is the operating system, installed software, package versions, configuration and hardware your result depends on.
The Turing Way, “Reproducible Environments” (CC BY 4.0) · see also xkcd 1987, “Python Environment”

For hydrology, conda-forge matters: GDAL, HDF5, netCDF and the mf6 executable are compiled libraries, not pure Python.
Speed is the new frontier: uv claims 10–100× faster than pip; pixi over 10× faster than conda (their own benchmarks).
29
An example environment
# environment.yml
name: hwrs564a
channels:
  - conda-forge
dependencies:
  - python=3.12
  - numpy
  - pandas
  - xarray
  - dask
  - matplotlib
  - jupyterlab
  - netcdf4
  - geopandas
  - rioxarray
  - flopy
  - modflow6 # mf6
conda (Miniforge)
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate hwrs564a
pixi
pixi init --import environment.yml
pixi run jupyter lab
uv (PyPI only, so fetch mf6 with FloPy)
uv init hwrs564a && cd hwrs564a
uv add flopy xarray dask netcdf4 jupyterlab
uv run get-modflow :python

31
When to reach for uv
A pure-Python project
uv init
uv add xarray dataretrieval
uv sync
Commit pyproject.toml and uv.lock; uv sync rebuilds it exactly
One analysis script
uv add --script gauges.py dataretrieval
uv run gauges.py
Dependencies live in the script’s header (PEP 723); uv builds a throwaway env
A specific Python
uv python install 3.12
uv venv --python 3.12
uv downloads Python itself: no system Python or pyenv needed
Speeding up pip
uv pip install -r requirements.txt
Same pip commands and files, much faster: good for older repos
One-off tools
uvx jupytext --to py lab.ipynb
Runs a tool in its own temporary env without touching yours
When not to use uv
Compiled tools and C libraries (e.g. GDAL command line)

33
Channels, lockfiles, containers
Channels
Use conda-forge through Miniforge: community-run, over 1 billion downloads a month by 2025.
Anaconda’s defaults channel has its own terms; university teaching and research are free, but conda-forge sidesteps the question.
Lockfiles
environment.yml says what you asked for. A lockfile records exactly what you got, for every platform.
pixi.lock, uv.lock, conda-lock, and Python’s new pylock.toml standard .
Containers
Docker packages the operating system layer too.
On UA HPC, use Apptainer (formerly Singularity), which can build from a Docker image. Binder builds a session from environment.yml.
Reproducibility is layered: environment file, then lockfile, then container. Go as far as your result needs.
34
Containers: the machine in a file
Dockerfile
The recipe: a base OS plus your environment
→
Image
Built once, in layers, with a version tag
→
Registry
GitHub Container Registry or Docker Hub
→
Container
A running copy: laptop, HPC, cloud, Codespaces
# Dockerfile: the course environment on a small Linux base
FROM mambaorg/micromamba
COPY --chown=$MAMBA_USER:$MAMBA_USER environment.yml /tmp/environment.yml
RUN micromamba install -y -n base -f /tmp/environment.yml && micromamba clean --all --yes
Environment vs container
An environment pins packages. A container also pins the operating system, system libraries and tools like mf6.
On UA HPC: Apptainer
apptainer build hw.sif docker://ghcr.io/OWNER/hwrs564a
apptainer exec hw.sif python model.py

Dev container
Move the computer to the data: NOAA and NASA publish petabytes on commercial clouds, including remote sensing datasets (MODIS, LandSat, etc), and forecasting/climate simulations (GEFS, CMIP6, etc).
How GitHub Codespaces works
1 · Repo
Your code plus .devcontainer/ devcontainer.json
→
2 · Build
GitHub builds that container on a cloud VM, 2 to 32 cores
→
3 · Codespace
Your clone in /workspaces; files persist between sessions
→
4 · Connect
VS Code in the browser or on your desktop, or JupyterLab
Stops
After 30 minutes idle (adjustable), and after 12 hours at most
Deleted
After 30 days stopped, unless you change the retention period
Free quota
120 core-hours and 15 GB a month; Pro: 180 and 20 GB
